newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers seek protection for medical devices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers seek protection for medical devices.

text.p: A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers Wednesday said they are introducing legislation that would limit the product liability of manufacturers of raw materials used in certain medical devices.

Under current law, makers of those "biomaterials" used in such devices as pacemakers, heart valves, angioplasty catheters and artificial joints can be sued under product liability laws even if they are not involved with the design or production of the device itself.
The bill would limit their liability to situations when they are directly at fault.

Backers of the bill say makers of these raw materials are beginning to shy away from the medical device marketplace, finding better markets in other industries such as the automotive or textile industries.

"Seven and one-half million Americans owe their lives to implantable medical devices," said Pennsylvania Republican Representative George Gekas, one of the sponsors. "The availability of these devices is in jeopardy because suppliers have ceased to supply raw materials and component parts ot medical implant manufacturers."
Gekas said the bill would not affect ongoing breast implant lawsuits.
